bay-5.uses: Rich in vitamins A and C, iron, calcium, and minerals; crushed leaf extract boosts moisture retention when applied to dry, sun-sensitized skin.
bay-5.description: A fast-growing annual herb with mealy gray-green diamond-shaped leaves.
bay-5.habitat: Steppe margins, gardens, and fertile stream-side soils in Bayburt.

gir-1.name: Coltsfoot
gir-1.uses: High leaf mucilage forms a protective film over respiratory epithelium to soothe bronchitis. Creates a moisture-retaining barrier on flaky dry skin.
gir-1.description: A perennial herb blooming in early spring with bright yellow flowers before broad heart-shaped leaves appear.
gir-1.habitat: Damp stream beds, embankments, and clay soils in Giresun.

gir-2.name: Black Elderberry
gir-2.uses: Cyanogenic glycosides and flavonoids in flowers and berries induce perspiration and reduce fever. Its infusion serves as a facial toner tightening pores and evening skin tone.
gir-2.description: A deciduous shrub or small tree with flat-topped creamy-white flower clusters and dark purple berries.
gir-2.habitat: Coastal and valley forest edges and humus-rich humid sites in Giresun.

gir-3.name: Lemon Balm
gir-3.uses: Rosmarinic acid and citral calm the central nervous system and relieve spasms. Its antiviral potency helps inhibit cellular replication of cold-sore (herpes) virus.
gir-3.description: A perennial aromatic herb with heart-shaped serrated leaves releasing a fresh lemon scent when crushed.
gir-3.habitat: Hazelnut orchard edges and shaded moist valley bottoms in Giresun.

gir-4.name: Syrian Juniper (Andız)
gir-4.uses: Resin and volatile oils from its cones relieve asthma and bronchitis symptoms via high terpene content. Its tar dries fungal, scabies, and eczema skin lesions.
gir-4.description: An evergreen juniper with sharp needle-like foliage and large fleshy berry-like cones.
gir-4.habitat: Southern mountain passes and rocky forest clearings in Giresun.

gir-5.name: Wormwood
gir-5.activeCompounds: Absinthin, thujone, sesquiterpene lactones, essential oils
gir-5.uses: Absinthin stimulates bitter receptors to boost gastric and bile secretions. Its strong aromatic profile helps cleanse bacterial and parasitic buildup on the skin.
gir-5.description: A perennial herb covered in silky silvery hairs with finely divided leaves and intensely bitter aroma.
gir-5.habitat: Inland rocky slopes and open dry hillsides in Giresun.

gum-1.name: Deadly Nightshade
gum-1.uses: Atropine and scopolamine alkaloids block parasympathetic signaling to stop smooth-muscle spasms and severe pain; medical ointments locally numb aching muscle tissue (strictly under clinical supervision).
gum-1.description: A potent alkaloid-bearing perennial with brownish-purple bell flowers and glossy black berries.
gum-1.habitat: Shaded beech-spruce forest clearings and calcareous slopes in Gümüşhane.

gum-2.name: Black Henbane
gum-2.uses: Hyoscyamine suppresses central nervous signaling to raise the pain threshold. Topical infused oils help relieve localized rheumatic joint pain.
gum-2.description: An annual or biennial sticky-hairy herb with pale yellow flowers veined in dark purple.
gum-2.habitat: Steppe margins, stony ground, and highland valley slopes in Gümüşhane.

gum-3.name: Alder Buckthorn
gum-3.uses: Frangulin and anthraquinone glycosides in aged bark stimulate the colon to relieve chronic constipation. Decoctions applied externally inhibit fungal growth on skin.
gum-3.description: A thornless deciduous shrub with dark lenticel-spotted bark and small dark berries.
gum-3.habitat: Moist stream banks and subalpine woodland margins in Gümüşhane.

gum-4.name: Lenten Rose (Oriental Hellebore)
gum-4.uses: Helleborin strongly affects cardiac muscle and circulation; root extracts were used in folk medicine as an external wash to remove skin parasites, lice, and ticks.
gum-4.description: A winter-to-spring blooming perennial with palmately divided leathery leaves and nodding greenish-cream blossoms.
gum-4.habitat: Shaded mountain forest understories and damp slopes in Gümüşhane.

gum-5.name: Rusty Foxglove
gum-5.uses: Digitoxin and digoxin glycosides in its leaves increase cardiac contractility. Never applied to skin; processed industrially as an essential raw source for cardiology medicines.
gum-5.description: A tall biennial or perennial bearing dense spikes of rusty-brown tubular flowers.
gum-5.habitat: Zigana foothills, woodland clearings, and highland meadows in Gümüşhane.

ord-1.name: Mandrake
ord-1.uses: Potent tropane alkaloids in its roots desensitize the central nervous system to ease severe pain. Crushed root poultices are applied to rheumatic joints and deep non-healing wound edges.
ord-1.description: An ancient medicinal perennial with a ground-hugging rosette of broad leaves and a thick forked taproot.
ord-1.habitat: Coastal scrub slopes and open soils across Ordu.

ord-2.name: White Henbane
ord-2.uses: High hyoscine content relieves smooth-muscle cramps and spasms. Leaf distillates used as skin compresses provide localized numbness to suppress pain.
ord-2.description: A softly hairy annual or biennial bearing pale yellow bell-shaped flowers and petioled leaves.
ord-2.habitat: Stony wall bases, coastal slopes, and open terrain in Ordu.

ord-3.name: White False Hellebore
ord-3.uses: Veratrine alkaloids dilate blood vessels to lower blood pressure. Diluted extracts are applied externally for chronic psoriasis plaques and parasite-related rashes.
ord-3.description: A robust perennial up to 1 m tall with pleated broad leaves and panicles of greenish-white flowers.
ord-3.habitat: Highland pastures of Ordu (Perşembe and Çambaşı plateaus).

ord-4.name: English Ivy
ord-4.uses: Hederagenin saponins thin bronchial secretions to clear coughs. Stimulates subcutaneous lymph and blood circulation to break down cellulite and bring boils to a head.
ord-4.description: An evergreen climbing vine with dark green lobed leaves clinging to trunks and walls.
ord-4.habitat: Shaded humid forests, stone walls, and river valleys in Ordu.

ord-5.name: Purple Foxglove
ord-5.uses: Cardiac glycosides act directly on heart muscle in heart failure therapy. Not used dermatologically; dedicated strictly to pharmaceutical drug production.
ord-5.description: A striking biennial or perennial bearing one-sided racemes of purple-pink spotted bell blossoms.
ord-5.habitat: Cool woodland clearings and moist humus-rich slopes in Ordu.

riz-1.name: Valerian
riz-1.uses: Valerenic acid in its roots activates brain GABA receptors to relieve severe anxiety and insomnia, while calming stress-triggered skin rashes and itching.
riz-1.description: A perennial herb with pinnate leaves, fragrant pink-white umbels, and aromatic rhizomes.
riz-1.habitat: Stream banks, damp highland meadows, and cool forest edges in Rize.

riz-2.name: Garden Angelica
riz-2.uses: Furanocoumarins in roots and fruits stimulate gastric secretion and relieve gas and cramps. Boosts subcutaneous blood flow to nourish skin tissue and restore radiance.
riz-2.description: A stately hollow-stemmed perennial with large divided leaves and spherical greenish-white umbels.
riz-2.habitat: High wet valleys, stream margins, and misty plateaus in Rize.

riz-3.name: Bay Laurel
riz-3.uses: Cineole essential oil supports digestion and inhibits fungal growth. Laurel soap and fixed oil calm eczema lesions and deeply purify the scalp.
riz-3.description: An evergreen tree with glossy dark aromatic leaves and black single-seeded drupes.
riz-3.habitat: Coastal strip and mild lower valley slopes of Rize.

riz-4.name: European Mistletoe
riz-4.uses: Viscotoxin and lectins help regulate blood pressure and boost immune cell activity. Bath preparations made from extracts ease rheumatic pain and inflammation.
riz-4.description: An evergreen hemiparasitic shrub growing in spherical tufts on host trees with pearly-white berries.
riz-4.habitat: Upper branches of forest and orchard trees in Rize.

riz-5.name: Tea Plant
riz-5.uses: Rich EGCG and caffeine deliver strong antioxidant protection. Brewed compresses constrict under-eye capillaries, reduce puffiness, and balance excess skin sebum.
riz-5.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy serrated leaves and white blossoms, iconic to Eastern Black Sea agriculture.
riz-5.habitat: Rainy coastal slopes and acidic humus-rich terraces in Rize.

sam-1.name: Guelder Rose (Gilaburu)
sam-1.activeCompounds: Viopudial, chlorogenic & organic acids, vitamin C
sam-1.uses: Viopudial in its berries relaxes smooth-muscle spasms and eases kidney stone passage. High antioxidant and organic acid levels protect skin tissue from free-radical aging.
sam-1.description: A shrub with three-lobed maple-like leaves, flat white flower rings, and translucent red berry clusters.
sam-1.habitat: Humid stream banks and inland woodland margins in Samsun.

sam-2.name: Horseradish
sam-2.activeCompounds: Sinigrin glycoside, allyl isothiocyanate, vitamin C
sam-2.uses: Mustard oil released from root sinigrin strongly stimulates circulation; applied locally, it accelerates blood flow to help fade hyperpigmentation spots.
sam-2.description: A perennial with a deep fleshy white taproot, large dark green leaves, and white flower racemes.
sam-2.habitat: Kızılırmak and Yeşilırmak deltas and moist alluvial margins in Samsun.

sam-3.name: Shepherd's Purse
sam-3.uses: Peptides and tannins exert a vasoconstrictive hemostatic effect that stops internal and external bleeding, speeding clotting in superficial cuts and bruises.
sam-3.description: An annual herb with tiny white flowers and distinctive heart-shaped triangular seed pods.
sam-3.habitat: Plains, grassy meadows, and roadsides across Samsun.

sam-4.name: Redroot Pigweed
sam-4.uses: Contains high levels of squalene, protein, and minerals; its astringent action suppresses inflammation on irritated skin surfaces and supports tissue integrity.
sam-4.description: An erect annual herb with long-stalked oval leaves and dense greenish flower spikes.
sam-4.habitat: Field borders, coastal plains, and moist open soils in Samsun.

sam-5.name: Common Poppy
sam-5.uses: Rhoeadine alkaloid in petals offers mild calming relief for coughs and sleeplessness. Petal infusion acts as a soothing anti-redness toner for sensitive skin with visible capillaries.
sam-5.description: An annual wildflower with bristly stems and delicate crumpled scarlet petals.
sam-5.habitat: Grain field margins and sunny lowland meadows in Samsun.

tra-1.name: Cherry Laurel (Taflan)
tra-1.uses: Prunasin glycoside in leaves suppresses the cough center and helps balance blood sugar. Leaf infusions applied topically soothe itchy dermatitis and skin spasms.
tra-1.description: A signature Eastern Black Sea tree with glossy leathery evergreen leaves, upright white racemes, and dark purple edible fruits.
tra-1.habitat: Humid coastal forests and valley slopes in Trabzon (0–1,200 m).

tra-2.name: Eyebright
tra-2.uses: Iridoid glycosides and tannins dry mucosal inflammation. Used as a compress on delicate periorbital skin, it reduces puffiness, conjunctivitis symptoms, and edema.
tra-2.description: A delicate highland herb with toothed leaves and white blossoms marked with purple veins and a yellow eye-spot.
tra-2.habitat: High alpine pastures and moist mountain slopes in Trabzon.

tra-3.name: Bilberry (Likapa)
tra-3.uses: Anthocyanins and flavonoids reduce capillary permeability, protecting retinal vessels and elastic connective tissue against microvascular fragility and sagging.
tra-3.description: A dwarf mountain shrub with angular green twigs, urn-shaped blooms, and deep blue-black berries.
tra-3.habitat: Zigana, Uzungöl, and high mountain forest understories in Trabzon (1,200–2,400 m).

tra-4.name: Bitterwood (Quassia)
tra-4.uses: Quassin is among the bitterest known natural compounds, stimulating gastric juice and appetite. Applied as a scalp wash, it completely clears lice, nits, and dandruff.
tra-4.description: A medicinal tree prized in traditional apothecaries for its intensely bitter wood and bark.
tra-4.habitat: Documented medicinal wood species in Trabzon's traditional herbalist inventory.

tra-5.name: Pine Resin (Çam Sakızı)
tra-5.uses: Resin acids and turpentine balance stomach acidity and clear airways. Forms a natural aromatic barrier preventing wound infection and helping draw out embedded splinters.
tra-5.description: Aromatic natural oleoresin harvested from Scots pine and Oriental spruce trunks in Trabzon's mountain forests.
tra-5.habitat: Maçka, Çaykara, and the high conifer forest belt of Trabzon.

mar-6.name: Istanbul Crocus
mar-6.uses: Because it occurs only in a narrow belt around Istanbul, wild collection is strictly discouraged; its chief value lies in biodiversity heritage and habitat conservation.
mar-6.description: A perennial bulbous geophyte with slender grass-like leaves that opens vivid golden-yellow blooms in early spring.
mar-6.habitat: Moist heathlands and forest clearings in Aydos Forest and around Ömerli on Istanbul's Asian side.

mar-7.name: Keltepe Crocus
mar-7.uses: Restricted to a tiny mountain summit zone with no commercial harvest; serves as a flagship species for regional ecotourism and alpine conservation.
mar-7.description: A recently described, delicate bulbous geophyte blooming right after snowmelt in early spring.
mar-7.habitat: Cool subalpine meadows and rocky clearings around Keltepe (Kartepe) in Kocaeli's Samanlı Mountains.

mar-8.name: Uludağ Wild Onion
mar-8.uses: Contains natural antibacterial sulfur compounds typical of wild Allium species; valued locally for culinary heritage while requiring protection as a mountain endemic.
mar-8.description: A perennial endemic mountain onion bearing spherical purple-pink umbels atop slender cylindrical stems.
mar-8.habitat: Moist stony mountain slopes and alpine meadows on Mount Uludağ in Bursa (1,000–2,100 m).

mar-9.name: Kazdağı Cushion Thyme
mar-9.uses: Rich in aromatic essential oils used traditionally in herbal infusions and scent, though wild harvesting must be avoided due to its restricted mountain range.
mar-9.description: A dwarf endemic thyme forming tight cushions across alpine rock faces with tiny fragrant leaves and pink-violet blooms.
mar-9.habitat: High rocky ridges and wind-swept limestone and metamorphic slopes of Mount Kazdağı in Balıkesir.

mar-10.name: Istanbul Wild Allium
mar-10.activeCompounds: Volatile sulfur compounds, phenolic acids, steroidal saponins
mar-10.uses: Surviving in fragmented island and coastal pockets, it is studied primarily as an indicator species for urban biodiversity protection and botanical education.
mar-10.description: A slender perennial bulbous plant opening pale purplish-white flower clusters in mid-summer.
mar-10.habitat: Restricted coastal maquis and rocky natural pockets in Istanbul and the Princes' Islands.

mar-11.name: Kilyos Knapweed
mar-11.uses: An emblematic endemic of Istanbul's Black Sea coastal dunes, vital for stabilizing coastal sand against erosion and guiding dune conservation initiatives.
mar-11.description: A dune-adapted perennial herb with felted gray-green leaves and showy pink-purple flower heads.
mar-11.habitat: Black Sea coastal sand dunes along Kilyos, Terkos, and Şile in northern Istanbul.

mar-12.name: Çatalca Knapweed
mar-12.uses: A strictly protected priority species with an extremely narrow range in the Thrace–Istanbul corridor, representing irreplaceable regional genetic heritage.
mar-12.description: A rare endemic knapweed with upright stems, narrow leaves, and delicate yellow-to-pink flower heads.
mar-12.habitat: Dry grasslands and woodland clearings around Çatalca on Istanbul's European side.

mar-13.name: Marmara Mullein
mar-13.uses: While mulleins are traditionally known for soothing coughs and throat irritation, this island-restricted endemic requires strict protection rather than wild harvest.
mar-13.description: A biennial plant marked by dense velvety silver leaves and tall spikes of bright yellow flowers.
mar-13.habitat: Sun-drenched rocky slopes of the Marmara Islands and Southern Marmara shores in Balıkesir.

ege-6.name: Aydın Fig
ege-6.activeCompounds: Ficin enzyme, dietary fiber, potassium, polyphenols, benzaldehyde
ege-6.uses: Fresh and dried figs regulate bowel motility and ease digestive complaints, while the proteolytic ficin enzyme in its milky latex has long been applied in folk remedies for warts.
ege-6.description: A broad-crowned deciduous tree with deeply lobed leaves, milky sap, and sweet pear-shaped syconium fruits famous across the Menderes basin.
ege-6.habitat: Büyük Menderes Valley, terraced hillside orchards, and mild river valleys of Aydın.

ege-7.name: Aegean Olive
ege-7.activeCompounds: Oleuropein, hydroxytyrosol, oleic acid, squalene, vitamin E
ege-7.uses: Cold-pressed olive oil protects cardiovascular health with monounsaturated fats and polyphenols; leaf infusions help balance blood pressure and blood sugar, while oil nourishes skin.
ege-7.description: An evergreen heritage tree with gnarled trunks and silvery-backed lance leaves capable of living for millennia.
ege-7.habitat: Sun-baked calcareous slopes across Aydın, Edremit, and the Aegean coastal belt (0–700 m).

ege-8.name: Turkish Oregano (Bilyalı Kekik)
ege-8.uses: Rich in carvacrol for potent antibacterial, antifungal, and antioxidant activity; consumed as tea or essential oil to ease respiratory infections, throat irritation, and digestion.
ege-8.description: A woody-based aromatic perennial subshrub bearing tight rounded clusters of tiny white flowers.
ege-8.habitat: Limestone slopes and terraced oregano fields of Denizli and the Aegean uplands.

ege-9.name: Opium Poppy (Afyon)
ege-9.activeCompounds: Morphine, codeine, papaverine, noscapine alkaloids; linoleic oil
ege-9.uses: Poppy capsules supply regulated pharmaceuticals with essential analgesic alkaloids, while its nutritious seeds and cold-pressed oil are staples in traditional Aegean pastries and spreads.
ege-9.description: An annual crop with waxy blue-green leaves, large white-to-violet petals, and rounded seed capsules.
ege-9.habitat: Licensed agricultural plains of Afyonkarahisar and the Inner Aegean plateau (900–1,200 m).

akd-6.name: Kasnak Oak
akd-6.uses: Tannin-rich bark and acorns served in traditional hemostatic preparations and leather tanning, while its straight, elastic timber was prized for bentwood hoops and cooperage.
akd-6.description: A majestic endemic Anatolian oak reaching 25–30 meters with deeply lobed broad leaves and a straight trunk.
akd-6.habitat: Kasnak Oak Nature Reserve near Eğirdir (Isparta) and Sultan Mountains forests (1,300–1,800 m).

akd-7.name: Taurus Mountain Tea
akd-7.uses: Brewed for centuries across Mediterranean highlands as an aromatic winter tea to strengthen immunity, ease colds, and calm digestive discomfort.
akd-7.description: An endemic Taurus mountain tea with woolly silvery foliage and upright spikes of pinkish-purple flower whorls.
akd-7.habitat: Calcareous rocky slopes of the Western Taurus highlands around Alanya and Akseki in Antalya (1,000–2,000 m).

akd-8.name: Mediterranean Jerusalem Sage
akd-8.activeCompounds: Iridoid glycosides, phenylethanoid glycosides, essential oils
akd-8.uses: Infusions and poultices prepared from its leaves are applied in folk medicine to soothe stomach upsets, stimulate appetite, and speed superficial wound healing.
akd-8.description: A Mediterranean shrub with large velvety leaves and tiered whorls of bright golden-yellow hooded blooms.
akd-8.habitat: Red pine forest clearings and calcareous maquis hillsides across Antalya and the western Mediterranean.

akd-9.name: Watt's Crocus
akd-9.uses: Strictly protected due to its tiny autumn-blooming distribution on Mount Tahtalı; wild harvesting is prohibited and it serves as a flagship Lycian conservation species.
akd-9.description: An autumn-flowering endemic crocus displaying lilac-veined petals and vivid scarlet stigmas before foliage emerges.
akd-9.habitat: Stony limestone clearings in cedar forests around Kemer and Mount Tahtalı in Antalya.

akd-10.name: Alpine Taurus Cyclamen
akd-10.uses: Its tubers contain toxic saponins and must never be ingested; protected against wild digging and studied botanically for ornamental and pharmacological traits.
akd-10.description: A late-winter geophyte pushing reflexed magenta-pink blooms and silver-marbled rounded leaves through melting snow.
akd-10.habitat: High mountain slopes and cedar forest understories in Burdur and the Western Taurus (1,000–2,000 m).

akd-11.name: Gazipaşa Rock Oregano
akd-11.uses: Known from only a handful of limestone cliffs between Alanya and Gazipaşa; studied scientifically for its essential oil chemotype while requiring strict cliffside protection.
akd-11.description: A cliff-dwelling endemic oregano producing graceful drooping spikes of rose-pink bracts and small hairy leaves.
akd-11.habitat: Sheer limestone crevices between Alanya and Gazipaşa in Antalya province.

akd-12.name: Holy Mediterranean Orchid
akd-12.uses: Historically prized for glucomannan-rich tubers used in hot salep and Maraş ice cream; today all wild orchids are strictly protected from harvest by national law and CITES.
akd-12.description: An elegant Mediterranean terrestrial orchid raising dense rose-purple flower spikes in spring from paired tubers.
akd-12.habitat: Sunny calcareous meadows and maquis openings from Kahramanmaraş foothills to the Mediterranean coast.

akd-13.name: Tumble Thistle (Kenger)
akd-13.uses: Young shoots are cooked in regional dishes; hardened latex harvested from root cuts forms traditional Kenger chewing gum for gum health and digestion, while roasted seeds make a caffeine-free coffee.
akd-13.description: A spiny perennial thistle with white-veined leaves and milky sap throughout its stems and heads.
akd-13.habitat: Taurus foothills above Çukurova and sunny rocky hillsides in Adana.

akd-14.name: Snowbell / Storax Tree
akd-14.activeCompounds: Egonol, benzoin resin, saponins, fixed oils
akd-14.uses: Fragrant resin from its bark has served since antiquity as incense, antiseptic expectorant, and skin salve, while its hard round seeds are strung into traditional prayer beads.
akd-14.description: A deciduous Mediterranean shrub bearing drooping clusters of fragrant pure-white flowers followed by hazelnut-like capsules.
akd-14.habitat: Maquis shrublands, canyon floors, and limestone slopes in Mersin and the Taurus foothills.

akd-15.name: Common Myrtle (Hambeles)
akd-15.uses: Aromatic berries are eaten fresh or pressed into syrups, while leaf infusions serve as antiseptic, blood-sugar-balancing, and respiratory remedies alongside skincare essential oil.
akd-15.description: An evergreen Mediterranean shrub with glossy aromatic leaves, starry white summer blossoms, and dusty blue-black berries.
akd-15.habitat: Coastal maquis, stream valleys, and forest edges across Mersin (which shares its Turkish name) up to 600 m.

akd-16.name: Caper Bush (Kebere)
akd-16.uses: Unopened flower buds are pickled as capers rich in capillary-strengthening rutin, while root bark preparations support liver and joint health in traditional medicine.
akd-16.description: A sprawling spiny shrub with fleshy rounded leaves and showy white flowers bursting with long violet stamens.
akd-16.habitat: Sun-baked rocky hillsides, dry stone walls, and cliffs in Burdur and inland Mediterranean valleys.

akd-17.name: Greek Strawberry Tree
akd-17.activeCompounds: Arbutin, ursolic acid, ellagic acid, flavonoids
akd-17.uses: Arbutin in its leaves provides urinary-tract antiseptic and skin-brightening effects, while vitamin C-rich berries and crimson peeling bark carry culinary and dye heritage.
akd-17.description: An unmistakable Mediterranean tree famed for smooth cinnamon-red peeling bark and glossy evergreen foliage.
akd-17.habitat: Limestone maquis slopes and red pine foothills across Antalya and the Western Taurus.

akd-18.name: Sticky Fleabane
akd-18.uses: Sticky resinous leaves are applied directly as traditional wound dressings to halt bleeding and prevent infection, alongside notable antifungal and insect-repellent activity.
akd-18.description: A vigorous autumn-blooming perennial covered in fragrant sticky resin glands and bright yellow flower heads.
akd-18.habitat: Roadsides, stony slopes, dry streambeds, and coastal plains in Adana.

akd-19.name: Syrian / Andız Juniper
akd-19.activeCompounds: Alpha-pinene, diterpene resin acids, volatile terpenes, natural sugars
akd-19.uses: Traditional "Andız Molasses" boiled from its large fleshy cones relieves cough, bronchitis, and fluid retention, while distilled juniper tar treats chronic skin lesions.
akd-19.description: A stately evergreen tree bearing prickly whorled needles and the largest plum-sized fleshy cones of any juniper.
akd-19.habitat: High calcareous mountain slopes of Kahramanmaraş and the Taurus Mountains (600–1,800 m).

akd-20.name: Summer Asphodel (Çiriş)
akd-20.uses: Tender spring shoots are cooked as a popular wild green in regional pies and sautés, while crushed fleshy root tubers form poultices for boils and skin blemishes.
akd-20.description: A robust perennial sending up tall branched panicles of pink-striped white starry flowers from basal leaf tufts.
akd-20.habitat: Stony pastures, foothills, and open maquis slopes across Isparta and the Mediterranean belt.

akd-21.name: Oleander
akd-21.uses: Highly toxic if ingested due to potent cardiac glycosides and strictly unsafe for home tea; scientifically studied for oleandrin's cardiac and oncological mechanisms, and used externally in historical ointments.
akd-21.description: An evergreen streamside shrub with leathery lance-shaped leaves and vibrant clusters of pink or white summer blooms.
akd-21.habitat: Seasonal gravel streambeds, canyon floors, and coastal gullies throughout Hatay and the Mediterranean coast.

akd-22.name: Anatolian Pomegranate
akd-22.activeCompounds: Punicalagin, ellagic acid, anthocyanins, pelletierine alkaloids
akd-22.uses: Juice and sour pomegranate molasses deliver potent antioxidants for cardiovascular and immune health, while tannin-rich dried rinds are decocted to stop diarrhea and gargled for sore throats.
akd-22.description: A long-lived fruiting shrub displaying scarlet trumpet flowers and thick-rinded fruits packed with ruby arils.
akd-22.habitat: Sunny fertile orchards and foothills around Osmaniye and the Eastern Mediterranean plains.

dog-6.name: Yarrow (Civanperçemi)
dog-6.activeCompounds: Chamazulene, achilleine, volatile oils, flavonoids, tannins
dog-6.uses: Infusions support digestive comfort and ease menstrual cramps, while fresh crushed feathery leaves act as a classic folk styptic to stop bleeding and heal minor wounds.
dog-6.description: An aromatic perennial bearing finely divided fern-like leaves and flat-topped corymbs of white or pale pink florets.
dog-6.habitat: High meadows, pastures, and plateau roadsides across Erzurum (1,400–2,600 m).

dog-7.name: Syrian Rue (Üzerlik)
dog-7.uses: Burned for millennia in Anatolian incense and folk protection rituals; due to potent beta-carboline alkaloids, external compresses target joint pain while internal ingestion is avoided.
dog-7.description: A bushy steppe perennial with deeply cut fleshy leaves, white five-petaled blossoms, and three-chambered seed capsules.
dog-7.habitat: Arid stony steppes and dry foothills across Malatya and Eastern Anatolia.

dog-8.name: Patience Dock (Evelik)
dog-8.activeCompounds: Anthraquinone derivatives, oxalic acid, vitamin C, iron, potassium
dog-8.uses: Beloved in Eastern Anatolian cuisine for stuffed leaf rolls and herb soups; rich in iron and fiber to relieve constipation, while leaf poultices calm skin inflammation.
dog-8.description: A hardy perennial dock featuring broad wavy-margined basal leaves and tall reddish-green flowering spikes.
dog-8.habitat: Moist stream banks, village pastures, and fertile meadows around Lake Van.

dog-9.name: Giant Mountain Fennel (Çaşur)
dog-9.uses: Young spring stems are parboiled or brined in traditional Erzincan dishes; locally prized to aid digestion, balance blood sugar, and boost physical vitality.
dog-9.description: A tall mountain perennial with finely feathery dill-like foliage and broad golden-yellow umbels.
dog-9.habitat: High rocky steppe slopes of the Munzur and Keşiş Mountains in Erzincan (1,600–2,700 m).

dog-10.name: Pennyroyal Mint (Yarpuz)
dog-10.uses: Collected along mountain streams and dried for traditional infusions and culinary seasoning to relieve colds, nausea, and digestive cramps; its pungent scent repels insects.
dog-10.description: A spreading streamside mint with strongly fragrant small leaves and dense violet-lilac flower whorls.
dog-10.habitat: Wet stream margins, springs, and cool valley meadows across Bingöl.

dog-11.name: Foxtail Lily (Gulik / Çiriş)
dog-11.uses: Cherished in Tunceli as "Gulik", its tender spring shoots are cooked in healing greens and pies to boost immunity and diuresis, while root poultices ease rheumatic aches.
dog-11.description: A striking mountain geophyte emerging with succulent rosettes and towering spires of greenish-yellow blooms.
dog-11.habitat: High rocky pastures of the Munzur Mountains, Ovacık, and Pülümür in Tunceli (1,300–2,600 m).

dog-12.name: Black Henbane
dog-12.uses: Potently toxic if ingested due to tropane alkaloids; historically used externally for toothache vapor and harvested pharmaceutically for antispasmodic medicines.
dog-12.description: A sticky-hairy biennial herb with deeply toothed leaves and lurid cream-yellow flowers veined in deep purple.
dog-12.habitat: Highland pastures, stony waste ground, and plateau margins in Kars.

dog-13.name: Milk Thistle
dog-13.uses: Silymarin in its seeds protects and regenerates liver cells against toxins, widely used in teas and extracts to support liver function and ease indigestion.
dog-13.description: A tall biennial thistle easily recognized by white-marbled spiny leaves and vivid purple flower heads.
dog-13.habitat: Sunny field edges, valley floors, and steppe clearings in Elazığ.

gun-6.name: Karacadağ Crocus
gun-6.uses: A rare early-spring endemic of the volcanic Karacadağ massif; protected from wild digging and monitored as a flagship regional biodiversity species.
gun-6.description: A perennial endemic crocus blooming in shades of pale blue-violet to cream amidst dark volcanic basalt.
gun-6.habitat: Volcanic slopes and rocky upland meadows of Mount Karacadağ in Diyarbakır.

gun-7.name: Mesopotamian Squill
gun-7.uses: Confined exclusively to limestone crevices along the Euphrates River; strictly protected from collection under species recovery and Halfeti ecotourism conservation programs.
gun-7.description: A crevice-dwelling bulbous endemic opening racemes of starry blue-violet blossoms in early spring.
gun-7.habitat: Shaded limestone cliff fissures around Halfeti and the Euphrates Canyon in Şanlıurfa.

gun-8.name: Gaziantep Milk-Vetch
gun-8.uses: A deep-rooted steppe endemic vital for preventing soil erosion; while related species yield tragacanth gum, this localized Gaziantep endemic is prioritized for habitat protection.
gun-8.description: A cushion-forming spiny endemic milk-vetch with pinnate leaves and creamy-yellow pea-like blossoms.
gun-8.habitat: Arid limestone hills and rocky steppe slopes around Gaziantep.

gun-9.name: Gaziantep Savory
gun-9.uses: Studied in phytochemistry for potent antimicrobial and antioxidant essential oils; due to its narrow local range, cultivation is encouraged over wild harvesting.
gun-9.description: A woody-stemmed perennial savory with narrow aromatic leaves and small white-to-pink flowers.
gun-9.habitat: Calcareous rocky hills and warm dry hillsides around Gaziantep.

gun-10.name: Aintab Dame's Rocket
gun-10.uses: Releases a sweet evening fragrance to attract nocturnal pollinators; cherished in biodiversity surveys as a strictly protected limestone endemic of the Kilis–Gaziantep frontier.
gun-10.description: An upright hairy perennial bearing four-petaled lilac-violet flowers whose scent intensifies at dusk.
gun-10.habitat: Shaded limestone crags and scrubby slopes in Kilis along the southern Anatolian foothills.

gun-11.name: Haussknecht's Knapweed
gun-11.uses: Found only in restricted southern calcareous steppes and not harvested; holds high conservation value for drought-tolerant genetic biodiversity.
gun-11.description: An endemic knapweed with gray-tomentose divided foliage and rosy-purple flower heads cradled in spiny bracts.
gun-11.habitat: Dry limestone slopes, stony margins, and warm steppe habitats in Kilis.

gun-12.name: Green-Flowered Fritillary
gun-12.uses: A rare bulbous endemic strictly protected against digging or ingestion; prized in botanical conservation for its unusual greenish-yellow nodding bell flowers.
gun-12.description: A slender endemic fritillary bearing solitary nodding bell-shaped blooms of pale yellowish-green.
gun-12.habitat: Rocky scrublands and oak woodland clearings along the Kilis and Amanos transition zone.

gun-13.name: Bornmüller's Golden-Drop
gun-13.uses: Deep red shikonin pigments extracted from its root bark were traditionally infused into salves to heal burns and deep wounds, as well as serving as a natural crimson dye.
gun-13.description: A bristly-hairy endemic bearing drooping creamy-yellow tubular blooms above a deep crimson-dyed root.
gun-13.habitat: Mount Nemrut foothills and sunny limestone slopes in Adıyaman (800–2,000 m).

gun-14.name: Mesopotamian Gundelia
gun-14.uses: A narrow-range endemic cousin of the traditional culinary tumble-thistle, valued in ethnobotanical conservation as a distinct regional genetic lineage.
gun-14.description: An endemic thistle distinguished by purplish flower clusters, cobwebby spiny bracts, and milky sap.
gun-14.habitat: Stony foothills and dry steppes across Siirt and the Upper Tigris basin.

gun-15.name: Showy St. John's Wort
gun-15.uses: Rich in oil glands containing hypericin and flavonoids similar to medicinal St. John's wort, yet conserved in the wild due to its localized southeastern limestone distribution.
gun-15.description: A striking perennial endemic bearing large golden-yellow flowers fringed with black-dotted sepals.
gun-15.habitat: Limestone crags, stony slopes, and oak clearings in Mardin.

ica-6.name: Yanardöner (Ankara Cornflower)
ica-6.uses: Found naturally nowhere else on Earth except around Lake Mogan in Gölbaşı, Ankara; strictly protected by law as a national botanical conservation emblem.
ica-6.description: An annual endemic famous for funnel-shaped petals that shimmer iridesently from crimson to violet-pink in sunlight.
ica-6.habitat: Calcareous field margins around Lake Mogan in Gölbaşı, Ankara.

ica-7.name: Ankara Crocus
ica-7.uses: Heralded as the classic herald of spring across Central Anatolian steppes; historically noted in regional lore while today safeguarded as an endemic geophyte.
ica-7.description: An early-blooming perennial crocus opening vibrant golden-orange flowers as soon as winter snow recedes.
ica-7.habitat: Steppe slopes, scrub clearings, and upland pastures around Ankara (900–1,600 m).

ica-8.name: Anatolian Steppe Sage
ica-8.uses: Brewed in Central Anatolian plateaus as an antiseptic mountain tea against colds, sore throats, and digestive spasms.
ica-8.description: A cushion-forming endemic sage with silvery foliage and violet florets nestled inside papery pink-tinted calyces.
ica-8.habitat: Mount Erciyes foothills in Kayseri and volcanic or gypsum steppes of Central Anatolia (1,000–2,200 m).

ica-9.name: Anatolian Highland Thyme
ica-9.activeCompounds: Citral, geraniol, thymol, carvacrol, rosmarinic acid
ica-9.uses: Used across high Anatolian steppes as a soothing expectorant tea and culinary herb, while providing prized nectar for mountain honeybees.
ica-9.description: A mat-forming aromatic subshrub hugging rocky ground with tiny fragrant leaves and pale rose-lilac flower heads.
ica-9.habitat: High gypsum and limestone steppe ridges across Sivas (1,100–2,300 m).

ica-10.name: Dwarf Everlasting (Altın Otu)
ica-10.uses: Papery golden blossoms stimulate bile flow, assist kidney stone passage, relieve bloating, and supply anti-aging flavonoids in botanical skin oils.
ica-10.description: A woolly steppe perennial crowned with papery bright golden flower heads that retain color when dried.
ica-10.habitat: Dry sandy steppe slopes and open pine woodland margins around Yozgat.

ica-11.name: Common Hawthorn (Alıç)
ica-11.activeCompounds: Oligomeric procyanidins (OPCs), hyperoside, vitexin, vitamin C
ica-11.uses: Leaves, blossoms, and crimson berries strengthen cardiac muscle contraction, dilate coronary vessels, and balance blood pressure through teas and traditional hawthorn vinegar.
ica-11.description: A thorny deciduous shrub bearing deeply lobed leaves, fragrant white spring blossoms, and single-seeded red haws.
ica-11.habitat: Steppe hillsides, scrubby valleys, and stream banks in Kırşehir (800–1,700 m).

ica-12.name: Tartar Breadplant
ica-12.activeCompounds: Glucosinolates, sinigrin, vitamin C, sulfur compounds
ica-12.uses: Fleshy starch-rich roots historically served as famine food and folk immune support; today protected as a declining relict of undisturbed Anatolian chalk steppes.
ica-12.description: A large steppe perennial with massive divided cabbage-like leaves that sends up clouds of tiny white blossoms.
ica-12.habitat: Undisturbed calcareous steppes of the Konya Obruk Plateau and Karapınar plains.

ica-13.name: Cilician Cyclamen
ica-13.uses: A fragrant autumn-flowering endemic prized in botanical conservation; its saponin-rich tubers are toxic if eaten and strictly protected from wild collection.
ica-13.description: A delicate endemic geophyte opening fragrant pale-pink blooms with magenta bases alongside heart-shaped leaves.
ica-13.habitat: Shaded rocky woodland understories in Niğde's Aladağlar and the Central Taurus (1,000–2,000 m).

ica-14.name: Rough St. John's Wort
ica-14.uses: Flowering stems are brewed or macerated in olive oil across highland Central Anatolia to soothe stomach ulcers, gallbladder discomfort, and inflammation.
ica-14.description: A tough perennial St. John's wort marked by rough reddish stems and dense flat clusters of golden-yellow flowers.
ica-14.habitat: Dry stony uplands and Taşeli steppe transitions in Karaman (1,200–2,400 m).

tr.header.subtitle: TÜRKİYE COĞRAFİ BİTKİ ENVANTERİ
tr.banner.title: Türkiye Etnobotanik Haritası
tr.banner.desc: Ülkemizin 7 coğrafi bölgesinde yetişen özel/endemik bitki türlerini keşfetmek için haritaya tıklayın.

tr.drawer.comingSoonDesc: Şimdilik araştırılan 8 Karadeniz ilindeki (Artvin, Bayburt, Giresun, Gümüşhane, Ordu, Rize, Samsun, Trabzon) toplam 40 tıbbi bitkiyi haritadan seçerek inceleyebilirsiniz.

tr.about.purposeDesc: Ülkemizin 7 coğrafi bölgesinde yetişen endemik ve özel bitki türlerini herkesin keşfedebilmesini sağlamak. Anadolu'nun binlerce yıllık bitki kültürünü dijital dünyaya taşıyoruz.
tr.about.howDesc: Haritadaki bölgelere tıklayarak bitkileri keşfedin. Her bitkinin QR kodunu yazdırıp okuldaki veya doğadaki panolara yerleştirebilir, telefonla okutarak detaylı bilgiye ulaşabilirsiniz.
tr.about.whyDesc: Türkiye, Avrupa'nın en zengin bitki çeşitliliğine sahip ülkelerinden biridir. 12.000'den fazla bitki türünün yaklaşık 3.000'i endemiktir. Bu mirası korumak ve tanıtmak hepimizin görevidir.

tr.stats.subtitle: Anadolu topraklarının sakladığı doğal hazineler

tr.guide.step3Desc: QR Kod Baskı Sayfası'ndan kodları yazdırıp panonuza yerleştirin.

en.header.subtitle: GEOGRAPHICAL PLANT INVENTORY OF TÜRKİYE
en.banner.title: Ethnobotanical Map of Türkiye
en.banner.desc: Click on the map to explore endemic and special plant species growing across Türkiye's 7 geographical regions.
en.drawer.selectProvinceHint: Click any highlighted province on the map or below to view its recorded medicinal plants.
en.drawer.comingSoonDesc: Explore all 40 medicinal plants recorded across the 8 researched Black Sea provinces (Artvin, Bayburt, Giresun, Gümüşhane, Ordu, Rize, Samsun, Trabzon).
en.drawer.comingSoonGenericDesc: Ethnobotanical documentation for this province is in progress. Select any active province in this region below:
en.search.placeholder: Search plant, Latin name, province or region...
en.search.noResults: No plants, provinces, or regions matched your search.
en.drawer.subtitle: Endemic and native plant species of this region are listed below. Click for details and QR codes.
en.about.purposeDesc: Making it possible for everyone to discover endemic and special plant species across Türkiye's 7 geographical regions. We bring Anatolia's millennia-old botanical heritage into the digital world.
en.about.howDesc: Click regions on the map to explore plants. You can print each plant's QR code for school or nature boards and scan it with a phone to view full botanical details.
en.about.whyDesc: Türkiye has one of the richest plant diversities in Europe. Out of more than 12,000 plant species, roughly 3,000 are endemic. Protecting and sharing this heritage is everyone's responsibility.
en.stats.title: Plant Diversity of Türkiye
en.stats.subtitle: Natural treasures hidden in Anatolian soil
en.stats.quote: "Türkiye possesses a botanical richness nearly equal to the total number of plant species found across the entire European continent."
en.guide.title: How to Use the Map?
en.guide.subtitle: Discover Anatolian flora in 3 simple steps
en.guide.step1Desc: Choose a geographical region directly on the map or from the colored badges above.
en.guide.step2Desc: Select a plant from the drawer list or map pins to read its ethnobotanical details.
en.guide.step3Desc: Print the codes from the QR Code Print Sheet and place them on your exhibition board.
en.plant.notesDesc: Active compound analyses (flavonoids, alkaloids, tannins) and student research notes compiled for this species will appear here.
en.plant.consDisclaimer: This indicator is an educational assessment prepared according to the species' endemism and rarity.
en.plant.qrDesc: This QR code links directly to this plant's dedicated profile page.
en.qr.title: QR Code Print Sheet
en.qr.subtitle: Print QR codes for all plants on the map and place them onto your 7-region geographical map board.
en.footer.desc: An ethnobotanical inventory platform enabling you to explore Türkiye's endemic and special plant species on an interactive map.
en.footer.infoDesc: This platform was developed to showcase Türkiye's plant biodiversity and raise conservation awareness.
